checked: 2026-10-10, by hand. Sources: every non-basic source against its oracle text (unchanged from the verdict-era golden, which listed the same cards). Pips: a plain symbol tally of the 63 nonland cards (the 99 less 36 lands) and the commander (W 18, R 26, G 56; 17, 25, 55 without the commander). Patterns: a second tally with its own regex, no shared parser, for W, R and G. Tapped lands: read from each land's text, the three categories separately. Karsten figures: the 99-card column of Frank Karsten, 'How Many Sources Do You Need to Consistently Cast Your Spells? A 2022 Update' (TCGplayer), as Hugh pasted it.
notes: Pips with the commander: Gishath, Sun's Avatar is {5}{R}{G}{W}, one each of R, G and W. Without it Deckcheck's own Gishath figure reproduces: green is 55 of 97 colored pips, 56.7%. The deck has no U or B pip and no hybrid pip.

Another color's pips are generic mana for this one. The commander is 7C for green (eight mana value, one green pip): the table has no row for it, so it would show a ceiling of 14, but green has six harder patterns and only the six hardest are listed, so it is not among them. The Tarrasque ({6}{G}{G}{G}) is 6CCC, past the table's 4CCC, and shows a ceiling of 26. Wakening Sun's Avatar is 5CCC for white, also a ceiling of 26.

The commander appears in a color's pattern list as a card, marked '(commander)'. Shatterskull Smashing // Shatterskull, the Hammer Pass is counted as a spell (CC for red) because its front face is a spell.

Sources follow the Colors card's own policy: an any-color source with a spending restriction counts for each deck color, a land that fetches a basic counts for the basics it can fetch, Farseek names Plains, Island, Swamp and Mountain so it counts for W, U, B and R and not G. U and B each read 1 source (Farseek) against 0 pips.

Tapped lands: 4 always = Jungle Shrine, Path of Ancestry, Mosswort Bridge, Spinerock Knoll (each says it enters tapped). 5 unless a condition holds = Clifftop Retreat, Rootbound Crag, Sunpetal Grove, Canopy Vista, Cinder Glade. 4 fetch a tapped land = Evolving Wilds, Fabled Passage, Escape Tunnel, Sheltering Landscape: each enters untapped itself and puts a basic onto the battlefield tapped (Fabled Passage untaps it with four or more lands). Counting the four fetches as tapped lands, as an earlier version did, called Evolving Wilds a land that enters tapped.

Karsten lands 42.2 = 31.42 + 3.13 x 4.34 - 0.28 x 10. Average mana value 4.34 counts the 63 nonland cards and the commander (8) as one more card, which reproduces Deckcheck's 4.34. Cheap ramp is 10: ten mana sources of mana value 3 or less (draw spells are not counted). Deckcheck reports 6 ramp and 38 lands for the same deck; this engine counts 36 land cards.

Help, add green: no Plains or Mountain may move. The guard keeps a color that meets Karsten's figure for its hardest published pattern at or above it, and a color below it from losing a source. White has 26 sources against 26 for 2CC (Lightmine Field), so a Plains out drops it under; red has 27 against 30 for CC (Shatterskull Smashing), so a Mountain out is a loss while under; blue and black hold no basics. Rebalance is therefore empty. Trades and staples depend on the collection and the commander index and are printed by the eval and not pinned.

karstenHardest is Karsten's figure for the hardest of ALL a color's patterns that has a published row: white 26 (2CC, Lightmine Field), red 30 (CC, Shatterskull Smashing), green 28 (1CC, three cards). The patterns listed are the six hardest by pips and may hide a lower published row; this figure does not.
